collectors-of-1961-nucards-horror-monste.core: Posted in last 7 days Collectors Of 1961 Nu-Cards Horror Monsters - Blue-Border Examples Anyone here collect 1961 Nu-Cards Horror Monsters? Especially the blue-border cards? I've been researching the 1961 Nu-Cards Horror Monsters set for an article on Cards Mania. The set has quite a few unusual details. Some first-series cards were distributed in perforated panels, later packs advertised invisible "Ghost Gum," and card #102 has a particularly scarce redemption-back variation. I also found a 1962 legal article documenting Universal Pictures' copyright case against Nu-Cards. The court proceedings are more substantial than I'd expected from the usual hobby summaries. One thing I'm particularly curious about is the blue-border issue. Some collectors describe those cards as prototypes, while Kurt Kuersteiner has argued they could be unauthorized copies. The obscured Nu-Cards address on the backs is an interesting detail. Here's the article with the sources and some recent auction results: https://cardsmania.fun/1961-nu-cards-horror-monsters/ Does anyone here own a blue-border example or know of documentation connecting them directly to Nu-Cards? I'd be interested in seeing it. Cards Mania

I am a UK-based Master’s Journalism student (and member of the community) working on a nuanced piece about generational trauma in African families for my final project. Moving beyond stereotypes, this project explores the roots of these cycles, including colonial history and a lack of mental health resources and highlights those working to break them and heal. Who I’m Looking To Speak With: UK-based adults raised by African parentswilling to share how these dynamics have affected their mental health and adult lives. former-redpill-followers-leaving-manosph.headline: Former Red-Pill Followers - Leaving Manosphere Anonymously
former-redpill-followers-leaving-manosph.author: Sea-Isopod-1678
former-redpill-followers-leaving-manosph.core: Posted in last 7 days Former Red-Pill Followers - Leaving Manosphere Anonymously TV documentary looking to speak to former 'red-pill' followers – completely anonymously Hi everyone, I'm a TV producer working for the UK broadcaster Sky. We're currently making a documentary about how young men's insecurities and anxieties can sometimes be exploited by influential figures in the 'manosphere', and how this can lead young people towards increasingly extreme or controversial views. Crucially, our documentary is being told from the perspective of young men themselves. We're not interested in vilifying or judging anyone who has been drawn into the manosphere. Instead, we want to understand what makes this content appealing in the first place, how it can gradually shape someone's beliefs, and why it can sometimes be difficult to recognise what's happening. We're particularly keen to speak to someone who, when they were younger, became involved in red-pill communities or adopted some of those beliefs, but has since moved away from that ideology. We think there's a really important message here for our younger viewers: that people who get caught up in these communities aren't inherently 'bad' people, that it's possible to find yourself adopting beliefs you might never previously have agreed with, and, most importantly, that it's possible to find a way out. We'd love to hear about your experiences, what originally attracted you to this world, what eventually made you question those beliefs, and how your perspective has changed since. Any interview would be entirely anonymous. We would not identify you in the documentary, and we'd be very happy to explain exactly how we'd protect your identity before you agreed to take part. If this sounds like something you might be interested in, please drop me a private message. There's absolutely no obligation to take part, and I'd be happy to answer any questions. Many thanks! Sky
